cf.title: Warn when creating or enabling a subscription with max_logical_replication_workers = 0

input.subject: Warn when creating or enabling a subscription with max_logical_replication_workers = 0

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a or 1b: the problem is stated, the cost falls only on misconfigured servers, and reviewers found the warning useful. The one surviving objection, maintenance-fit-1, is a fixable design point about where the check lives. Message #13 already shows a gap between CREATE and ALTER ... SET (retain_dead_tuples), so a committer would likely ask for one shared test of whether the launcher runs.

brief.title: Warn on create or enable subscription when max_logical_replication_workers is 0
brief.problem: With max_logical_replication_workers = 0 the logical replication launcher never starts, yet CREATE SUBSCRIPTION and ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... ENABLE succeed silently. Users then wonder why replication does not start. The author reports user reports of this confusion.
brief.proposed_design: CREATE SUBSCRIPTION and ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... ENABLE emit a WARNING with a HINT when max_logical_replication_workers is 0. The check sits in subscriptioncmds.c, next to existing messages such as "subscription was created, but is not connected". Running out of worker slots when the setting is above 0 is out of scope.
user_visible_surface: New WARNING on CREATE SUBSCRIPTION: "subscription was created, but logical replication is disabled".
New WARNING on ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... ENABLE: "subscription was enabled, but logical replication is disabled".
New HINT: "To initiate replication, set "max_logical_replication_workers" to a non zero value."
The CREATE SUBSCRIPTION warning also fires with enabled = false and retain_dead_tuples = true.
author_claims: Users today get no sign from these commands that replication cannot start.
Users have reported confusion over this behaviour.
Warning only for the 0 case is enough, because with a value above 0 the launcher logs "out of logical replication worker slots".
A backend check of free worker slots needs new infrastructure and an LWLock, and its result can change before the worker starts.
brief.thread_state: Peter Smith, Hou zj and Dilip Kumar asked for a warning based on available workers; the author declined, and two reviewers (Shubhra Jain, João Rito) tested the February patch and accept the narrow scope. Open items: a rebase, a test, hint wording for retain_dead_tuples, ALTER ... SET (retain_dead_tuples) coverage, and Rafia Sabih's separate pg_stat_subscription_stats counter proposal.
unclear: The patch has no regression or TAP test, and no updated version was posted after February.
The proposal does not say whether ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... SET (retain_dead_tuples) should warn, though CREATE warns for the same option.
The proposal does not cover max_worker_processes = 0, where the launcher is also absent and commands succeed silently.
The proposal does not cover a server restarted with the setting changed to 0 after subscriptions exist.
The proposal does not say whether any documentation changes.

out of logical replication worker slots

objections.title: Warning condition copied into command sites, so it drifts from launcher.c
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a subscription option that needs the launcher, or changes when the launcher registers. The patch author updates launcher.c and calls ApplyLauncherWakeupAtCommit(), but does not add the new check in subscriptioncmds.c. Users on a server with the launcher absent then get silence again, and no test fails.
objections.argument: The check tests max_logical_replication_workers directly in subscriptioncmds.c, while ApplyLauncherRegister() in launcher.c decides on its own conditions (message #5). The gaps already exist. Message #13 shows that ALTER ... SET (retain_dead_tuples) does not warn and that max_worker_processes = 0 is silent. Peter Smith raised the other callers in message #9, and the author kept the per-site approach in message #10. No test exercises the path, so drift will not show up.
objections.author_must_show: Can the decision whether the launcher will run come from one function in launcher.c, so that new callers and new registration conditions cannot miss the warning?

critic.reasoning: Message #13 shows the drift already exists: CREATE warns for retain_dead_tuples, but ALTER ... SET (retain_dead_tuples) does not. Peter Smith's question in message #9 about other ApplyLauncherWakeup() callers was answered by keeping the per-site check, and no test covers the path.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The warning reports that the logical replication launcher will not start on the subscriber; no WAL or protocol behaviour changes.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: A restore that runs CREATE SUBSCRIPTION with retain_dead_tuples = true on a server with the setting at 0 may emit the new warning.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The check in subscriptioncmds.c repeats a condition that launcher.c decides, and no test covers it.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Can one function in launcher.c report whether the launcher will run, so that every command site uses the same test?
Should ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... SET (retain_dead_tuples) warn, given that CREATE SUBSCRIPTION warns for the same option?
Should the warning also cover max_worker_processes = 0, where the launcher is also absent and the commands succeed silently?
Will the next version add a regression or TAP test that fails when a command site misses the warning?
Does a pg_dump restore of a subscription with retain_dead_tuples = true emit the warning on a server with the setting at 0, and is that intended?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows the logical replication launcher and subscription commands would have to own it; the visible thread and CommitFest entry show no committer engaged.
committability.liability: Two new message strings and a check that must stay in step with the launcher registration conditions in launcher.c for as long as those conditions change.
committability.author_follow_up: The author answered review in February and moved the entry in August, but posted no new version after February and the patch needs a rebase since October.

priority.reason: The patch touches one file and only helps users who set max_logical_replication_workers to 0, which message #6 calls rare. It needs a rebase, a test and an answer on where the check lives before a committer can take it.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the exact warning conditions, the behaviour during a pg_dump restore, and how the check relates to ApplyLauncherRegister() could not be confirmed. Only 3 of 13 messages were shown in full.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improving the latch handling between logical replication launcher and worker processes.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes a lost wakeup in the logical replication launcher, which uses one latch for worker attach, worker exit and subscription creation, so a new subscription's apply worker can wait up to 180 seconds to start. The author listed three options and posted v2 using a separate latch for worker attach and exit, protected by a lock and owned only around each wait.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not state a closing reason. Kyotaro Horiguchi objected to v2 because it calls OwnLatch and DisownLatch often and nests latch waits across concurrent wakeup sources, and he proposed a flag in shared memory that ApplyLauncherMain checks before WaitLatch. The author agreed and posted a new patch for that approach, and Heikki Linnakangas noted that his proposed interrupts patches would make the fix simple. The thread ends there without a review of the new patch.

out of logical replication worker slots
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Additionally, handling multiple concurrently operating trigger sources with nested latch waits seems bug-prone, which I’d prefer to avoid from both a readability and safety perspective.

precedents_retrieved.title: Reuse Workers and Replication Slots during Logical Replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets a tablesync worker, after it finishes one table, pick up the next table in init state and sync it, keeping its replication slot. This removes the cost of starting a new worker and creating and dropping a slot for each table, which matters most for many empty or small tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Benchmarks by reviewers showed regressions in some settings, and the v28 design #2 results were up to about twice as slow as HEAD and varied widely between runs. The patch also no longer applied to HEAD. Amit Kapila proposed Returned with feedback because the regressions still needed analysis, and vignesh C asked for a new entry with a fix for the regression.

IIRC, there were some regressions observed with this patch. So, one
needs to analyze those as well.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve logicalrep_worker_launch() logic
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes logicalrep_worker_launch() so it also runs garbage collection of worker slots when the per-subscription parallel apply worker limit is reached, as it already does for the sync worker limit. It also reuses the slot that garbage collection just freed, instead of scanning all worker slots again.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amit Kapila argued that the parallel apply case is not a clear bug, because the apply worker applies changes itself when no parallel apply worker is available. He asked for a test case that reproduces the problem rather than a change based on reading the code. The thread ends with that request unanswered, and the entry was withdrawn about eight months later. No message states the reason for the withdrawal.
matched_queries: out of logical replication worker slots
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
No, the idea was that if we are changing the code, it is better to
test it via a testcase instead of changing based on assumptions.

precedents_retrieved.title: Warning for Datatype mismatch between subscriber table and publisher table for logical replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes logical replication emit a warning when a subscriber table column has a different data type from the matching publisher column. The goal is to show type mismatches early so users can debug replication problems.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author did not revise the patch after review, and it had not passed CI since about mid March, so the CF entry was closed. Ashutosh Bapat had asked for the unrelated file renames to be removed. He also noted that the code maps columns by position, and that it compares type OIDs and names on the subscriber without using the remote type cache.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Since this has not been fixed, and the patch has not passed CI since at least
mid March, I'll close this CF entry.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert logical snapshot filename format change in SnapBuildSnapshotExists().
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert logical snapshot filename format change in SnapBuildSnapshotExists().
Reverted commit(s): Standardize LSN formatting by zero padding
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 2633dae2e48 standardized LSN formatting but mistakenly changed
the logical snapshot filename format in SnapBuildSnapshotExists() from
"%X-%X.snap" to "%08X-%08X.snap". Other code still used the original
"%X-%X.snap" format, causing the replication slot synchronization worker
to fail to find existing snapshot files and produce excessive log messages.

This commit restores the original "%X-%X.snap" format
in SnapBuildSnapshotExists() to resolve the issue.

precedents_retrieved.title: transaction statistics of logical replication subscription
precedents_retrieved.summary: The thread first proposed counting failed transactions and their sizes in pg_stat_replication_slots, so that users could tell successful logical decoding from repeated failed attempts. By the last version, the patch instead added apply_commit_count and apply_rollback_count columns to pg_stat_subscription_stats.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amit Kapila noted that pg_stat_database already shows committed and rolled-back transactions per database, so the new counters largely duplicate it, and he asked whether anyone saw value in them. Masahiko Sawada agreed that commit and rollback counts without transaction sizes no longer meet the original goal and have no concrete use case. The author then marked the entry Returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
But I’m concerned that adding only apply_commit_count
and apply_rollback_count ends up adding the duplicate statistics with
no concrete use cases.

precedents_retrieved.title: logicalrep_worker_launch - counting/checking the type limits
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes logicalrep_worker_launch() so it checks only the worker limit for the type being launched: the tablesync limit for tablesync workers and the parallel apply limit for parallel apply workers. It also applies the same garbage-collection retry to parallel apply workers that tablesync workers already get, and fixes a copied comment in logicalrep_sync_worker_count().
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry after a long period without activity. Amit Kapila asked whether the garbage-collection condition could be reproduced and whether a crashed leader worker would restart the server anyway, and the author never answered. The entry moved to Waiting on Author, and the author withdrew it when the commitfest manager asked him to answer or withdraw.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Did you try to reproduce this condition, if not, can you please try it
once? I wonder if the leader worker crashed, won't it lead to a
restart of the server?

precedents_retrieved.title: Logical replication timeout
precedents_retrieved.summary: A walsender spent hours unlinking every possible spill file name for a large transaction in ReorderBufferRestoreCleanup, so the subscriber timed out and decoding restarted in a loop. The patch records which WAL segments a transaction actually spilled to, so cleanup removes only those files.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last shown message, in March 2025, only reports a rebase. A reviewer had also asked for a second patch that sends progress updates during long loops such as cleanup, and no message shows that patch.

precedents_retrieved.title: ALTER TABLE: emit NOTICE when ONLY is omitted but no partition recursion occurs
precedents_retrieved.summary:
ALTER TABLE: emit NOTICE when ONLY is omitted but no partition recursion occurs
Threads: ALTER TABLE: warn when actions do not recurse to partitions

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. The only listed row, [P24], is about an ALTER TABLE notice on partition recursion and has no recorded reason, so it shares only the general idea of adding a notice. The thread does not point to any earlier discussion of a warning for max_logical_replication_workers = 0.

From the standards and compatibility angle, the proposal adds no syntax, GUC, catalog or dump change. It follows the existing "subscription was created, but is not connected" message pattern, so existing scripts and dumps keep working. Hint wording and the missing warning on ALTER ... SET (retain_dead_tuples) are open items already raised in messages #12 and #13. Without the code, I could not check whether a pg_dump restore with retain_dead_tuples = true into a server with the setting at 0 triggers the new warning.

The patch adds only a WARNING and HINT in subscriptioncmds.c. It changes no catalog, WAL record, on-disk format, wire message or extension API, so nothing affects pg_upgrade, standbys or subscribers. The publisher slot that CREATE SUBSCRIPTION leaves inactive with the setting at 0 exists today, and the warning makes it easier to notice. Rafia Sabih's pg_stat_subscription_stats counter would change persisted stats, but it is a separate proposal.

The proposal has no real privilege or exposure aspect. The new warning reports the value of max_logical_replication_workers, which any user can already read with SHOW, and only users allowed to run CREATE or ALTER SUBSCRIPTION see it. The proposal adds no new privilege, no new code path that runs user-controlled code, and no new resource use.
Apart from this point, the maintenance cost is small. It is one file, adds no cost to any hot path, and adds no GUC, catalog or API. Ten such warnings per release would be acceptable.

Message #1 names the existing way, checking pg_stat_subscription (empty pid) or pg_stat_replication, but users only check once they suspect a problem, and a command-time WARNING costs little and falls only on this case. No extension or general hook covers this, and the patch reuses the existing "subscription was created, but is not connected" message pattern instead of adding a second mechanism.

Demand evidence is thin: message #1 cites unquantified user reports, and message #6 calls the 0 setting rare. Still, the cost is one check on the CREATE and ENABLE paths, seen only by misconfigured users, and three reviewers (messages #7, #12, #13) found it useful, so a show-demand objection would not hold.
